posted_text:
💰 AK HB193 — Alaska Could Require Employers to Offer Paid Sick Time

Alaska is considering a new law that would require employers with five or more employees to provide paid sick leave to their workers.

Employees would accrue at least one hour of paid sick time for every hour worked, up to a maximum of 40 hours per year, unless their employer sets a higher limit.

The rules would apply to all employees, including those exempt from overtime, and allow accrued sick time to roll over to the next year.

This new provision also addresses federal income tax withholding for paid parental leave benefits and adjusts unemployment benefit allowances for dependents.
